translations.text: Generosity is nobler than any art a person has in his whole body; a share of generosity in a person hides all blemishes.
There is no kin-slaying or treachery, no surliness, refusal or meanness, nor any wrong a person does, that generosity does not completely cover.
Plunder and the wounding of a person, an outcry of bells, an outcry of churches, an outcry of glass [?], greed, treachery, kin-slaying done fiercely [?]: generosity drowns all of that.
"It is well for me," says the generous man, "since I gave out my food; it is a light [?] to the King of the elements that my sense did not go backward."
"It is bad for me," says the stingy man; "the King of the heavens is displeased with me. Like everyone's nut, I have fallen from the tree [?]. Though I am badly off here, I will be worse there."
A well drained down to its gravel bed [?] has water that is none the worse for it. So it is with the storehouse from which many are fed.
When a person sets his hand to hospitality, his portion comes back to him exactly: for the single one [?] that he feeds properly, twelve come with the little brown one [?].
I am holy Columba, son of Fedlimid, from Inis Fáil [Ireland]. I pray to God, who shaped my face, that no one may take away my honour. Generosity.
